**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Always measure the pnpm store used by the frozen install**

When `npm_config_store_dir` is already set in the remote environment, this array measures that custom directory instead of `$HOME/.local/share/pnpm/store`, but the frozen install still explicitly writes to `$HOME/.local/share/pnpm/store` at line 2175. Growth in the actual install store is therefore omitted from `reserve_gate_bytes`, causing the receipt to understate disk consumption and later gates to be admitted with too little reserve; include the fixed install store even when a custom store is also present.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound each disk scan by the remaining gate hold time**

When `du` stalls near the configured deadline, this direct `timeout 60` can keep the checkout lock for up to another minute because it is independent of `deadline`; GNU `timeout --help` confirms that it allows the command its specified duration. Unlike commands run through `step()`, all three new measurements bypass the remaining-hold calculation, so a gate with a short `BEELINK_GATE_MAX_HOLD`, or one whose install nearly consumes its budget, can exceed the advertised lock bound before the next step notices expiry.
